questions.stem: A delivery driver travels 8 km north, then 6 km east to reach a customer. What is the magnitude of the driver's displacement?
questions.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular, so we use Pythagoras' theorem: displacement = sqrt(8² + 6²) = sqrt(64 + 36) = sqrt(100) = 10 km. The distance travelled is 8 + 6 = 14 km (option c), which is the total path length. Displacement is always the straight-line distance from start to finish.

questions.stem: A jogger runs 3 laps of a 400 m athletics track, finishing where they started. What are the distance and displacement?
questions.explanation: Distance is the total path length: 3 × 400 = 1200 m. Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish — since the jogger returns to the starting point, displacement = 0 m. This clearly shows how distance and displacement can be very different.

questions.stem: A ball is kicked 20 m east and then 15 m west. What is the displacement of the ball?
questions.explanation: Taking east as positive: displacement = +20 + (-15) = +5 m, which is 5 m east. The distance would be 20 + 15 = 35 m (options a/b). Remember, displacement accounts for direction, so movements in opposite directions partially cancel. The ball ends up 5 m to the east of where it started.

questions.stem: When is the magnitude of displacement equal to the distance travelled?

options.text: Always — they are the same thing
Only when the object returns to its starting point
Only when the object moves in a straight line without changing direction
Never — displacement is always less than distance

questions.explanation: Distance equals the magnitude of displacement only when an object moves in a straight line without changing direction. In this case, the total path length is the same as the straight-line distance from start to finish. Option (d) is wrong because they can be equal. Option (a) is wrong because they differ whenever direction changes.

questions.stem: A GPS shows you are 3 km from your starting point, but your car's odometer shows you have driven 5 km. Which quantity does each device measure?

options.text: GPS measures distance; odometer measures displacement
GPS measures displacement; odometer measures distance

questions.explanation: The GPS calculates the straight-line distance from the starting point (displacement magnitude = 3 km). The odometer records the total path length along the road (distance = 5 km). This is a real-world example showing that distance is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.
